correctness.rationale: The two perpendicular supporting equations give Q=e^(iθ)(h(θ)+i h(θ+π/2)) and constant modulus R by summing squared supports. The support phase stays in a quadrant, so winding is one, and |ψ′−1|≤c<1 makes the angle map one-to-one. Squaring the valid supporting equation R cos(ψ−θ)=h(θ) yields cos(2ψ−2θ)=c cos(2θ). Equivalently the phase of e^(2iψ)−c gives 2θ up to an additive constant locally; invertibility makes the positive derivative the actual inverse Jacobian, not a sum over branches. Its real part decomposes as (1+P_c)/2. Fourier orthogonality proves both parities and rotation covariance; radius plus the second moment gives the two semiaxes and (only for c>0) the axis modulo π. For 0<c<1 the positive part of f−uniform lies at cos(2ψ)>c. With v=arccos c, the tangent half-angle formula is 4 arctan(((1+c)/(1−c))tan(v/2))=π+2arcsin c for the Poisson-kernel integral; the arc length is π−2arcsin c, giving TV arcsin(c)/π after the mixture factor. At c=0 the difference is identically zero (the strict positive-region description is only for c>0). The thin limit follows from the disk kernel concentrating at 0 in doubled angle, and the conditional local density δ P_c(δx)/(2π) tends pointwise to 1/[π(1+x²)] with integral one on each side of the limit, proving TV by Scheffé. The conditioning is on the Poisson component, not the entire mixture.

reproduction.evidence: Five axis examples and a rotated case; coordinate intersections, Jacobian, moments and ellipse inversion, plus TV quadrature (max error 1.02e-11). 200,000 simulated draws per case pass familywise 99% Hoeffding tolerance .00904914. evidence: Odehnal treats orthoptics as the right-angle case of isoptic loci. Cieślak–Mozgawa eq. (1.2) is the normal-angle forward map, reducing to h(t)e^(it)+i h(t+π/2)e^(it).

In the stated observable, the law on the circle is equivalent after doubling the angle to an equal mixture of uniform and wrapped Cauchy (the Poisson kernel); lifting the latter uses two equal sheets.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The wrapped Cauchy family is already standard; the substantive identification is that its half-mixture, not pure wrapped Cauchy or uniform measure, arises from uniformly oriented paired supports. Results about normals sampled by arclength or perpendicular lines with no orientation do not give this pushforward.

value.rationale: There is a natural inverse problem when only intersection angle and radius are observable: radius alone cannot separate ellipses, while the second harmonic does at fixed radius. The exact mixture says how much orientation information survives and gives a quantitative measure of departure from uniformity and the angular resolution scale for very slender ellipses. These are exact properties of a distinct sampling protocol, not a reparametrization of a known locus invariant.
